newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: French trade mission seeks business in Argentina. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: French trade mission seeks business in Argentina. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]

text.p: French Trade (corrects from Industry) Minister Yves Galland will visit Argentina this week heading a group of executives from more than 40 firms and banks seeking business opportunities, the French embassy reported Tuesday.
During his five-day visit starting Wednesday Galland will meet with President Carlos Menem, congressmen and other federal and provincial government officials.

The companies represented in the tour include Aerospatiale, Airbus, Banque Nationale de Paris, Societe Generale, Banque Paribas , Credit Lyonnais , Generale des Eaux, Renault, T Total and the autonomous port of Le Havre.
Several French banks operate in Argentina, Renault cars are made under license, and several French firms have taken advantage of Menem's privatization drive to invest in utilities.
Gas de France has a stake in natural gas distributor Metrogas, Electricite de France in energy utility Edenor and Lyonnaise des Eaux in water utility Aguas Argentinas.
Le Havre, one of France's largest ports, last year signed a cooperation agreement with Bahia Blanca, a major grain port south of Buenos Aires.
Galland plans to give a news conference Friday and then fly on Saturday to Chile and Brazil, a French embassy official said.
